identity.title: $\tau^2$-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment

problem.claim: Evaluate conversational agents in settings where both agents and users act on a shared, dynamic world.

gap.claim: Existing conversational-agent benchmarks mainly model single-control environments in which users are passive, unlike scenarios requiring active user participation.

contributions.claim: Introduces a Telecom dual-control domain modeled as a Dec-POMDP, testing tool-mediated agent–user coordination and communication.
Provides a compositional task generator for diverse, verifiable tasks with controlled complexity, plus a tool- and state-constrained user simulator.
Includes fine-grained ablations separating reasoning errors from communication/coordination errors.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish the benchmark through dual control: both the agent and user use tools to act in a shared environment.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant performance drops when agents move from no-user to dual-control settings, underscoring difficulty in guiding users.
The authors report that the benchmark supports controlled testing of agents required to reason and guide user actions.
The authors report that code, data, and a leaderboard are available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing benchmarks treat the user as a passive information provider.
Technical-support scenarios require users to help modify a shared world.
The paper introduces a dual-control Telecom environment, compositional tasks, a constrained user simulator, and error-focused ablations.
Experiments report a performance drop under dual control; the benchmark is presented as a controlled testbed with released code, data, and leaderboard.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark explicitly separates reasoning errors from communication/coordination errors through ablations.

lessons.interpretation: A decomposition of failure modes can make an evaluation more diagnostically useful than a single aggregate score.
lessons.application: Design evaluation analyses that isolate task reasoning from interaction or coordination failures.
lessons.exception: This decomposition may be unsuitable when the failure mechanisms cannot be operationally separated or when the task has no interactive coordination component.

unknowns: The abstract does not report benchmark scale, agent identities, quantitative scores, ablation outcomes, or evaluation conditions.
The abstract does not establish whether the proposed simulator improves fidelity quantitatively or whether the benchmark generalizes beyond Telecom.
